title: Pavlova
subtitle: Crisp meringue with a soft marshmallow centre, topped with cream and fruit
excerpt: A large disc of meringue baked low and slow: crisp on the outside with a soft, chewy centre. Topped with whipped cream and fresh berries. The centrepiece dessert of the British summer.

recipe.sourceNotes: Pavlova was created to celebrate the Russian ballerina Anna Pavlova during her tour of Australia and New Zealand in 1926. Both countries claim the invention. The dish became established in Britain through the mid-20th century and is now a standard at summer gatherings. The distinguishing feature from French meringue is the addition of cornflour and vinegar to the egg whites, which creates the characteristic marshmallow interior.

content.text: The bowl and whisk must be completely clean and free of any grease or the whites will not whip. Add the sugar a tablespoon at a time and whisk well between each addition: rushing this step produces a weeping meringue. The meringue is done when it is stiff and glossy and holds a firm peak. Leave in the oven to cool completely after baking.
Heat the oven to 150 C / fan 130 C / gas 2. Draw a 25 cm circle on baking paper. Flip the paper over and place on a baking tray.

Whisk the egg whites in a large clean bowl until they form stiff peaks. Add the caster sugar one tablespoon at a time, whisking well after each addition. Continue until the meringue is stiff, glossy, and holds firm peaks.
Sift in the cornflour. Add the vinegar and vanilla. Fold gently to combine.

Spoon the meringue onto the circle, building up the sides slightly higher than the centre to create a well. Bake for 1 hour 15 minutes until the outside is crisp and lightly coloured. Turn off the oven. Leave the meringue inside with the door closed until completely cool.
Whip the cream to soft peaks. Spoon over the meringue. Top with the strawberries and raspberries. Serve within 2 hours.
